cards.explanation: The answer is that God hopes each of them will turn from his wicked way. He says, “Perhaps when the people of Judah hear about all the calamity I plan to bring upon them, each of them will turn from his wicked way.” (Jeremiah 36:3) He warns them first so they have the chance to turn. A warning is a door left open.

The word is forgive, friends. God says, “Then I will forgive their iniquity and their sin.” (Jeremiah 36:3) Notice He puts the forgiveness right there beside the warning. The whole thing is built to end well if they turn.

The answer is Baruch son of Neriah. Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet, calls Baruch, and Baruch writes “…all the words that the LORD had spoken to Jeremiah.” (Jeremiah 36:4) One man talks and one man writes. I hope Baruch stretched his writing hand first.

The answer is True, and Jeremiah is plain about it. He tells Baruch, “I am restricted; I cannot enter the house of the LORD…” and sends him there on a day of fasting to read the words “…in the hearing of the people…” (Jeremiah 36:5-6) The prophet can't go, so the scroll goes in his place. The words still get in the door.

The word is anger, friends. Jeremiah says, “for great are the anger and fury that the LORD has pronounced against this people.” (Jeremiah 36:7) That's why this reading matters so much. He still hopes they'll bring their petition before the LORD and turn.

The answer is the scribe's chamber in the king's palace. Micaiah, Gemariah's son, “…went down to the scribe’s chamber in the king’s palace, where all the officials were sitting…” (Jeremiah 36:12) He goes there right after he hears the scroll. Then he reports to them all the words he heard Baruch read. (Jeremiah 36:13)

The answer is False. Nobody tells Baruch to stop. The officials send Jehudi with the message, “Bring the scroll that you read in the hearing of the people, and come here.” (Jeremiah 36:14) Then they ask Baruch to read it in their hearing, and he does.

The answer is that they turn to one another in fear. “When they had heard all these words, they turned to one another in fear…” (Jeremiah 36:16) Baruch reads, and the officials hear every word of it. Then they turn to one another, afraid. Fear is what the text reports.

The answer is True. After the reading, the officials say to Baruch, “Surely we must report all these words to the king.” (Jeremiah 36:16) They don't sit on it, friends. They go to the king in the courtyard and report everything. (Jeremiah 36:20)

The word is hide. The officials tell Baruch, “You and Jeremiah must hide yourselves and tell no one where you are.” (Jeremiah 36:19) That's the order they give the two men, friends. The text doesn't say where they hide, only that they're told to.

The answer is Jehudi, the man who carried the officials' message to Baruch. “Then the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe.” (Jeremiah 36:21) Jehudi fetches it and reads it aloud to the king. He's a busy man in this chapter.

The answer is that the king cuts them off and throws them in the fire, and it's hard to hear. “…as soon as Jehudi had read three or four columns, Jehoiakim would cut them off with a scribe’s knife and throw them into the firepot, until the entire scroll had been consumed by the fire.” (Jeremiah 36:23) He does it again and again until nothing is left. I think this is one of the heavy parts of the story.

The answer is False. “Yet in hearing all these words, the king and his servants did not become frightened or tear their garments.” (Jeremiah 36:24) The officials who heard the scroll earlier turned to one another in fear. (Jeremiah 36:16) The king and his servants don't react that way.

The answer is that they urge the king not to burn it. “…Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll…” (Jeremiah 36:25) These three speak up, friends. The king won't listen to them.

The answer is True. The three officials urge the king, and the text says “…he would not listen to them.” Then the king commands Jerahmeel, a son of the king, along with Seraiah and Shelemiah “…to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet.” (Jeremiah 36:25-26) The scroll is gone and now he wants the men who wrote it. But the next verse is coming.

The answer is the LORD. The verse says it plainly: “But the LORD had hidden them.” (Jeremiah 36:26) The king commands three men to seize Baruch and Jeremiah, and the LORD has hidden them. The officials had told the two men to hide back in verse 19.

The answer is to write the very same words on another scroll. The LORD says, “Take another scroll and rewrite on it the very words that were on the original scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah has burned.” (Jeremiah 36:28) A fire doesn't cancel the message. It's like a burnt batch, friends. The recipe is still good.
The answer is David's. The LORD says about Jehoiakim, “He will have no one to sit on David’s throne…” (Jeremiah 36:30) That's the consequence for burning the scroll. It's a serious word.

The answer is True. The LORD says about Jehoiakim, “…his body will be thrown out and exposed to heat by day and frost by night.” (Jeremiah 36:30) I think this one is heavy, friends, and I'll leave it at that. It follows the king's choice to burn the scroll.

The answer is his descendants and servants. The LORD says, “I will punish him and his descendants and servants for their iniquity.” (Jeremiah 36:31) The consequences reach past the king himself. His descendants and servants are named right alongside him.

The answer is False. Baruch wrote down all the words from the burned scroll, and the verse adds, “And many similar words were added to them.” (Jeremiah 36:32) The king burned the first scroll, and the next one came out with more words. Like a second batch, friends, with extra sprinkles.
